privacy_redaction.hardware_identity: Public copy: physical GPU model and UUID are withheld; architecture labels do not identify a particular supported profile.
privacy_redaction.provenance: Measurements are retained. Embedded signatures, source digests and byte counts describe the private original records unless explicitly labeled as public-copy digests.
privacy_redaction.usage: Redacted review material, not an unmodified calibration input or a hardware identity attestation.

archive_transformations.identity_note: Original SHA256 values identify raw pre-redaction bytes. Sanitized nested reports cannot be passed as --run-report; local original reports can.
archive_transformations.paths: Host paths replaced by explicit role placeholders.

cache_condition: Shared persistent filesystem/compiler caches retained. Each case has a separate preparatory short run before formal calibration. Not a controlled empty-cache experiment; cache/JIT state is not automatically verified by the estimator.

limitations: Padding budgets every output sequence to sequence_length; dynamic batch padding, shuffling and distributed sampling are not modeled.
No filtering, train/validation splitting, resampling or framework preprocessing is performed.
The exact count describes the supplied processed rows; source-framework execution and training-split provenance are not verified.
input_ids are used as supplied; their original tokenizer and template cannot be inferred.
Supervised tokens count nonignored labels at nonpadding positions before any causal loss shift.
Update timing includes accumulation-window prefetch and forward/backward/optimizer work; evaluation and checkpoint events are timed separately.
Allocator peaks include initialization, training and final saves; they are not total device usage.
Wall time includes observer instrumentation and checkpoint hashing, reported separately.
Changed weights are verified using sampled values per trainable tensor, not an exhaustive tensor comparison.
Dynamic batch shapes are recorded but are unsuitable for fixed-shape timing extrapolation.

assumptions: Configuration values are reconciled with the actual native Trainer and model.

Each 16-update holdout consumes 32 microsteps: 64 rows for microbatch 2, 32 rows for microbatch 1. It is not a long-run convergence evaluation.
No packing, periodic evaluation/checkpoint, multi-GPU, OOM boundary, or cross-hardware timing transfer is validated here.
Training data, dtype, framework kernel and shape are part of calibration identity; native pipeline extrapolation additionally assumes comparable cache and setup costs.
